title: From Passwords to Context: Building a Modern Identity Foundation
body_markdown:
How McDonald’s is modernizing identity services to strengthen security, simplify its architecture, and support access at global scale.


*By: Rob Williams, Manager, Cybersecurity Operations*


**Quick Byte**


- As McDonald’s technology ecosystem grows, modernizing identity services is critical to securely support more applications, users, and access scenarios at global scale
- By moving from legacy federation infrastructure to a centralized cloud identity platform, teams can apply smarter, context-aware access controls, and streamline authentication management
- The result is a more scalable identity foundation that strengthens security, simplifies access management, and supports a better user experience across the business


For a digital-first enterprise operating in more than 100 countries, securing access to corporate resources requires solutions that can operate at a global scale. At McDonald’s, our authentication team helps make that possible by managing, maintaining, and optimizing how users securely access the systems and applications they rely on every day.


At this scale, authentication is more than a security checkpoint. It’s part of the foundation that connects people to the applications they need while helping us apply consistent protections across a complex global technology environment. Modernizing that foundation gives us a more scalable way to strengthen security while supporting a streamlined user experience.


As our technology landscape has evolved, so have the expectations placed on our identity services. More cloud applications, more integration points, and a broader range of users require an approach that can adapt quickly while maintaining consistent protections. That reality has helped drive our modernization efforts.


Over the years, we have migrated legacy federation infrastructure to cloud-based identity services and adopted additional capabilities that help us strengthen access controls.


**The migration: Modernizing beyond legacy federation** A foundational step in expanding our modernization is migrating away from Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS). For years, AD FS served as the primary federation service connecting on-premises identities with external software-as-a-service (SaaS) offerings and internal web applications.


Although AD FS has been a reliable platform, maintaining highly available on-premises federation infrastructure introduces operational complexity, patching requirements, and additional infrastructure dependencies. At the same time, many of the capabilities that help organizations evaluate access risks, apply adaptive security controls, and manage application access consistently are now delivered through modern cloud identity platforms.


For our team, this effort was about more than replacing technology. It was about creating a foundation better suited to supporting a global enterprise with diverse applications, evolving security requirements, and users working in many different contexts around the world.


The work is helping us simplify our identity architecture while continuing to support a diverse global application environment.


In a global environment, this work requires more than changing an application’s federation endpoint. Each application can have different technical requirements, dependencies, and user needs. Our team considered the appropriate authentication protocol, access requirements, and migration approach for each application.


We also support users across different markets, business functions, and technology environments, each with unique access requirements and expectations. A solution that works for one application or user population may not be appropriate for another. Modernizing identity at McDonald’s requires balancing consistency and flexibility at significant scale.


That balance is central to the team’s approach: establish a consistent identity foundation while accounting for the technical and user requirements of individual applications.


One way this modernization supports a more adaptable identity foundation is through context-aware access controls.


**Context-aware access in action** Imagine an employee traveling to collaborate on a marketing initiative who needs to access corporate resources from a location they do not normally use. Rather than relying only on a username and password, our identity platform can evaluate additional context around the sign-in and determine whether additional verification is appropriate.


This scenario illustrates an important part of our approach: access decisions do not have to rely on a username and password alone. They can account for the context surrounding a sign-in and apply additional security controls when that context warrants them.


Context-aware access controls can consider multiple factors associated with a sign-in and apply additional safeguards when appropriate. This allows the team to strengthen protection when circumstances warrant it without treating every user, application, or sign-in in the same way.


For our team, the goal is not simply to add more authentication steps. It’s to apply the appropriate protection based on the application and the circumstances of the sign-in.


That philosophy becomes especially important in an organization with diverse user needs. Whether someone is accessing training resources, collaborating on a business initiative, or working with more sensitive information, the level of protection required may differ based on the context and risk of the activity. Context-aware controls help us apply security requirements that align to risk while supporting a positive user experience. The result is an approach that can strengthen protection without introducing the same level of friction into every access experience.


**Connecting authentication and authorization** Modernizing authentication also gives us an opportunity to make application authorization more consistent.


Together, authentication and authorization help us address two important questions: Does this sign-in meet our security requirements, and is this user authorized to access the application? Managing these controls through a centralized identity platform helps us promote consistency while accounting for the different requirements of applications and user populations.


This distinction matters at McDonald’s scale, where securely completing a sign-in is only one part of helping people access the right resources for their work.


**Building a secure and scalable identity foundation** Modernizing identity at McDonald’s is an ongoing journey. As we continue evolving our identity services, we are building a foundation designed to be both secure and seamless for our workforce.


What makes this work especially meaningful is the scale at which it operates. Every day, the decisions made by our authentication team help support employees across geographies, functions, and technology platforms.


The work requires the team to combine technical expertise with an understanding of different applications, users, and business contexts. That is what allows a shared identity foundation to support varied needs at global scale.


For McDonald’s, this work is ultimately about establishing an identity foundation that can evolve with our technology environment. A centralized, context-aware approach helps us strengthen protections, simplify how access is managed, and support secure experiences at global scale.
